title: Ge/ZnS Dual-Band Filter with Constricted Thickness Bounds [80-400 nm]
scientific_hypothesis: Constricting thickness initialization bounds to [80, 400] nm and reducing optimizer step size by 50% will prevent thickness overshoot observed in prior iteration, forcing the solver to optimize around resonant quarter-wave thicknesses and improve convergence toward the theoretical dual-band transmission limit.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack with dual-cavity resonance for two distinct passbands. Ge (high index ~4.0) and ZnS (low index ~2.2) provide sufficient index contrast for sharp spectral edges within 24-layer constraint.
proposed_topology: 22 explicit layers: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 substrate
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses optimized within [80, 400] nm bounds
Optimizer step size reduced by 50% from prior iteration
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds [80, 400] nm compatible with conventional IR deposition
Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave optical thickness principle for bandpass filters
expected_advantages: Tighter bounds prevent optimizer from exploring non-physical thickness regions
Reduced step size improves convergence near quarter-wave resonances
Maintains proven Ge/ZnS material system from prior successful iteration
known_risks: Overly restrictive bounds may prevent discovery of optimal non-quarter-wave solutions
Reduced step size may increase optimization iterations needed
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band transmission. Wavelength bands: transmit 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm; block 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm. All 22 layer thicknesses are optimization variables with bounds [80, 400] nm. Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave values (Ge ~205 nm, ZnS ~375 nm at 3300 nm reference). Use gradient-based and differential evolution optimizers with step size reduced by 50% from standard defaults. Evaluate coherent TMM across 2500-5000 nm spectrum. Score candidates by mean transmittance in passbands and blocking bands. No metal layers. Air incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directives: constricted thickness bounds to [80, 400] nm and reduced optimizer step size by 50% to prevent thickness overshoot observed in iteration_06 where some layers exceeded 490 nm.
